title: Commission champions the next generation of European Capitals of Culture
content:
On 10 September 2026, the European Commission adopted its proposal for the new legal framework of the European Capitals of Culture action from 2034 to 2047. It will be discussed with both the European Parliament and the Council.

The European Capitals of Culture ’s current legal framework will come to an end in 2033. EU institutions thus need to determine how the action will be set up as of 2034 and ensure the initiative remains relevant, inclusive and impactful until 2047.

Based on thorough consultation and evaluation, the European Commission submitted a proposal to ensure that:

  • the action remains accessible and in line with EU priorities and current global challenges
  • the action reinforces its EU dimension
  • the right tools are provided to follow and react to the cities’ progress in implementing their programme and to plan for their legacy
  • the action remains visible by enhancing communication tools and activities

    • The proposal wants to bring more people in, make the process simpler and ensure the longer-term legacy of European Capitals of Culture.

title: European Heritage Days 2026: protecting Europe’s heritage at risk
content:
The EU strives to preserve cultural heritage under all circumstances, as reflected in the EU preparedness union strategy. Across Europe, communities are finding diverse ways to respond to these pressures with the support of the European Union.

Throughout September and October, the European Heritage Days 2026 invites people across Europe, under the theme “heritage at risk: revive, resist, reimagine” to discover how communities are protecting, restoring and reimagining their heritage for the future.

The 2026 European Heritage Days highlight how communities and EU-supported initiatives are protecting and adapting cultural heritage in response to climate change, societal shifts and other forms of threats, including conflict.

Link to the European Heritage Days website.

As climate change increases pressure on cultural sites and landscapes through extreme weather, flooding, fires and other natural hazards, protecting heritage also means finding ways to adapt. These challenges highlight how closely Europe’s natural and cultural heritage are connected.

title: The 2026 European Union Prize for Literature anthology is out
content:
“European stories”, the 2026 European Union Prize for Literature (EUPL) anthology presents the 14 shortlisted EUPL authors from 2026 and showcases excerpts from their nominated books both in the original languages and in English translation.

The main purpose of the anthology is to present these 14 emerging and talented writers to the European publishing world, and to get them translated into other European languages. Some of the 2026 shortlisted authors have already signed translation deals following the prize ceremony on 29th of May at the Warsaw Museum of Modern Art.

The anthology will be distributed at major book fairs like Gothenburg and Frankfurt. The e-book version is also available online on the Office of Publications website for anyone to read.

The anthology features stories from the 14 shortlisted authors of the 2026 European Union Prize for Literature.

Link to the Publications Office of the EU.

The prize is an annual initiative of the Creative Europe programme. It started in 2009 to recognise the best European emerging authors and celebrate the linguistic diversity and excellence of literature in countries participating in the Creative Europe programme.

title: Open Call of Perform Europe 2026 – 2028
content:
After two highly successful editions (2020-2022 / 2023-2026), Perform Europe will continue to put emphasis on exploring, with the performing arts sector, how cross-border touring can be made fairer, greener, and more inclusive.

Proposals are submitted by collaboration partnerships of performing arts professionals and organisations. Partners should work on their proposal together. This is a call to the sector to create partnerships and propose impactful ideas that can generate real change via two main priorities:

  • Inclusion and diversity
  • Fight against climate change

    • Each proposal should choose one of the above main priorities to focus on, while still taking into account and implementing measures related to the second priority.

    In addition, all proposals should aim for quality and innovation, be built on fair practices, and are encouraged to promote collaboration across different regions within the 41 Creative Europe countries.

    The open call was launched on 23 June 2026. We invite you now to build partnerships, jointly develop proposals, and submit them through our website before 22 October 2026, 23:59 CEST.

    Perform Europe will grant €1.4 million to at least 25 partnerships.

title: European Commission publishes call for evidence on AI strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors
content:
The European Commission’s strategy will set out a vision to support the Cultural and Creative Sectors (CCS) while fostering innovation and safeguarding European cultural and linguistic diversity.

The opportunities and challenges presented by AI in the CCS are complex, spanning technical, economic and societal dimensions. This call for evidence aims to gather information and stakeholders’ views to help develop a strategy that will ensure AI complements, rather than replaces, human creativity; supports broader access to culture and knowledge; and contributes to a fair, sustainable, innovative and competitive European creative economy.

The consultation is open in all EU languages to anyone, including artists, creators, rights holders, professional associations, AI providers, developers, researchers and public authorities with cultural and AI policy expertise, as well as members of the public with an interest in the future of culture and creativity in the age of AI.

Help shape the future AI strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors with your views until 11 September 2026.

Link to the public consultation website of the European Commission.
